'''Charlie Will Bell III''' (born March 12, 1979) is an American professional former [[basketball]] player and coach. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]], and then played parts of eight seasons in the [[NBA]]. He also served as an assistant coach for the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/iowa-wolves-finalize-coaching-basketball-operations-staff/|title=Iowa Wolves Finalize Coaching and Basketball Operations Staff|publisher=Iowa Wolves|date=October 13, 2017 |access-date=October 13, 2017}}</ref> and as an assistant coach for the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]].

==High school==
Bell played high school basketball at [[Flint Southwestern Academy]] High School, in [[Flint, Michigan]].

==College career==
Bell had an excellent [[college basketball]] career at [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], appearing in three straight [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] [[Final Four]]s, and being named Michigan State Defensive Player of the Year in each of the four years he played there. He was a starter for the [[1999–2000 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Spartans]] in their [[2000 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2000 National Championship]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charlie Bell College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/charlie-bell-1.html |access-date=2024-12-16 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional playing career==
Bell wasn't selected in the [[NBA draft]], but he was signed by the [[Phoenix Suns]], on July 23, 2001, as a [[free agent]], and played five games for them. After being released by the Suns, he signed with the [[Phoenix Eclipse]] of the [[American Basketball Association (2000-)|ABA]] and played four games for them. He initially signed a 10-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on January 10, 2002, and was then signed for the remainder of the season on January 15, but only appeared in two games.

After a rather brief stint in the NBA, Bell took his career to [[Europe]] to play in the Italian and Spanish Leagues where he was regarded as a star. In March 2002, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]], of the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian League]], and he won the Italian League championship with Treviso. In the 2002–03 season, he played with [[Virtus Bologna|Virtus (Kinder) Bologna]], but he was injured in December 2002, and was sidelined for most of the season. In August 2003, he signed with [[Basket Livorno|Mabo Livorno]], also of the Italian League. In July 2004, he signed with [[CB Breogán|Leche Rio Breogan Lugo]], of the [[Liga ACB|Spanish League]], and he was named to the [[All-Liga ACB Team|All-Spanish League First team]] for the 2004–05 season. He was also [[ACB stats leaders|the top scorer of the Spanish league]], and he was a three time [[ACB Player of the Month|Spanish League player of the month]].

Bell signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the 2005–06 season, and on March 28, 2006, had his best performance since entering the league, recording his first career [[triple-double]] in the Bucks' 132–110 win over the Suns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bucks 132-110 Suns (Mar 28, 2006) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/260328015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411183006/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/260328015 |archive-date=April 11, 2022 |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Bell had then-career highs of 19 points, 13 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 10 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] to lead Milwaukee. Bell, who played only seven games in his prior NBA season in 2001–02, appeared in 59 games (starting in six) for the Bucks in the 2005–2006 regular season, and finished with averages of 8.4 points, 2.2 assists, and 2.0 rebounds in 21.7 minutes per game. That [[2006 NBA Playoffs|postseason]], Bell led the Bucks in scoring with a postseason career-high 13 points in 24 minutes of playing time during their first game, a 92-74 Game 1 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pistons 92-74 Bucks (Apr 23, 2006) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/260423008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231014185609/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/260423008 |archive-date=October 14, 2023 |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> The Bucks would end up losing the series four games to one.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/2006-nba-eastern-conference-first-round-bucks-vs-pistons.html 2006 NBA Eastern Conference First Round Bucks vs. Pistons]</ref>

The following [[2006-07 NBA season|season]], to 13 points, 3 rebounds and 3 assists per games in 35 minutes on average, while appearing in all 82 games.

On September 17, 2007, being a [[restricted free agent]], Bell signed an offer sheet from the [[Miami Heat]] worth $18,500,000 over five years.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/bell_070917.html HEAT: HEAT Sign Charlie Bell to Offer Sheet.<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Although he stated that he did not want to play for Milwaukee, they decided to match the offer three days later.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/CharlieBellSigns_070920.html BUCKS: Bucks re-sign Charlie Bell.<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On June 22, 2010, Bell, along with [[Dan Gadzuric]], was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] for [[Corey Maggette]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_bell_gadzuric_062210.html |title=Warriors Acquire Charlie Bell And Dan Gadzuric From Milwaukee |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 22, 2010 |access-date=June 23, 2010}}</ref> He was waived by the Warriors under the [[amnesty clause]] prior to the [[2011–12 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/12/11/warriors-bell.ap/index.html | title=Warriors waived Bell under new amnesty provision| work=NBA.com | publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc | date=December 11, 2011 | access-date=December 11, 2011}}</ref>

Bell's final NBA game was on February 22, 2011, in a 93 - 115 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]] where Bell played for only 2 minutes and recorded no stats.

In January 2012, he signed with [[Juvecaserta Basket|Pepsi Caserta]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/33891/charlie_bell_signs_in_italy_with_otto_caserta.html Charlie Bell signs in Italy with Otto Caserta.]</ref>

==Coaching career==
On November 3, 2016, Bell was hired by the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA Development League]] to be an assistant coach. Later, Bell was hired by the Iowa Wolves to become an Assistant Coach, this is where he will be for a few years.<ref>{{cite web|first=Britney|last=Wynn|url=http://texas.dleague.nba.com/news/legends-add-charlie-bell-coaching-bench-nbas-assistant-coaches-program/|title=Legends Add Charlie Bell to Coaching Bench from NBA'S Assistant Coaches Program|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2016|access-date=December 4, 2016}}</ref>

==Off the court==
Bell stars in a popular series of webisodes titled, '''"Hey Charlie, Do My Job!"''' in which he takes up a fan's occupation (e.g. working at [[Wendy's]], or being an [[interior decorator]]) for a day, and currently works for UWM (United Wholesale Mortgage) as an Account Executive.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/robdube/2019/05/27/what-playing-for-a-national-championship-winning-basketball-team-taught-this-ceo-about-leadership/?sh=347c343a7c91|title = What Playing For A National Championship Winning Basketball Team Taught This CEO About Leadership| website=[[Forbes]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/charlie-bell-4342619b/ |title=Charlie Bell  |website=[[LinkedIn]]}}</ref>
